**Whom a province obeys** (decided 31 October 2026, build order item 17++; Haakon: "Can province ownership be made into something more agnostic? As in not something you owned hardcoded, but something that abides you, by a combination of force and loyalty?", then "Yes, please, expertly!"). A province is not owned by a flag: each season it obeys whoever it fears or loves most. Fear is force: troops standing in it or near enough to answer it, weighed against its own men of fighting age ("The people defend their land"). Love is the ledger: its standing with each actor who has given or taken there. The one whose weight is greatest holds it; if nobody's weight clears what its people will accept, it obeys no one and is lawless ("Land without a ruler"). Every way a province changes hands is this one rule seen from a side: conquest is force tipping it; revolt is love for another outweighing fear of the master when his troops leave or are beaten ("Revolt follows conditions, not dice"); absorption is love growing behind the force; a governor turning is his standing outweighing his king's; succession is an heir inheriting only part of his father's standing ("A realm holds by its ledger"); and a ceded province obeys its new master only once his troops or his governor are there and he earns its standing, as cessions did. Obedience has degrees: a province held by a wide margin pays and levies in full, one held narrowly pays grudgingly and hides more ("The king says how much he wants" under The world), which the mood of the land shows ("Who holds what, and the mood of the land" under Interface). It does not flicker: standing and memory move slowly, the question is asked once a season, and a change of hands needs the new weight to exceed the old clearly; the seeded dice only settle exact ties at the margin. Every change of hands comes as news with its cause ("Gubla now answers to Aziru: his men stand at its gates, and Pharaoh has sent no grain in three years"). The ledger is the standing of the many: the provinces, their peoples and the rank and file of armies. Persons, kings, governors, vassals and every other character, do not obey a ledger but choose by their stakes, each playing to rank highest on the one scoreboard by the strategy his traits give him ("Stakes, not dispositions" under Characters): an agreeable man works from within the system, a bold one strikes out alone (Haakon: "Remember that character's foremost motivation is always to rank higher on the scoreboard, so loyalty doesn't factor into it in the same way for a character's, as it does for a non-player entity like a province. But if it is a character with agreeable traits, then teh chosen strategy for maximizing their score standing is an more conservative one that favors working from within the system."). So the ledger decides what a person can do, which provinces and men would follow him, and his strategy decides what he will do. A vassal is the same rule one level up: his provinces obey him, and he serves his overlord by his oath for as long as his own reckoning says it pays. First guesses for every weight, the floor and the margin, tuned in item 18.

**Revolt follows conditions, not dice** (decided 20 October 2026; read through the ledger from item 17++, decided 31 October 2026, Haakon: "Yes, fix all expertly!"). A province's unrest is how low its ledger stands with whoever holds it ("Loyalty is a ledger"): the ledger decides how far it leans away from him, and the moment decides when it rises, both from conditions the engine can see; the seeded dice only settle ties at the margin. The homeland too (decided 29 October 2026, build order item 17): land a power has fully absorbed starts loyal, its ledger long in credit, and needs far more to rise, so a home revolt is rare, but a king who keeps starving his own provinces can lose one. What decides it, each condition either an entry in the ledger or the moment:

- **How new the conquest is:** the ledger starts low with a new master and rises only as he gives, which is the land's absorption;
- **hardship:** famine or another catastrophe there, levies raised from it, gold taken from it, and troops taking its food, by how much they took, its own king's included (decided 29 October 2026), each an entry against whoever took;
- **the master's weakness:** his armies beaten, his capital besieged, his troops busy elsewhere: not an entry in the ledger but the moment, when a low standing becomes a rising;
- **distance:** far from the king, by the measure of item 7, since the people credit the hand they see;
- **a cause to rally to:** the province's old ruler alive and free, or a character of standing there who wants it, whose own ledger there may stand higher than the master's: the moment, and a man to lead it;
- **outside help:** a rival's gold, which enters the ledger as his giving, or his envoys and armies promising support, which make the moment; deniable like any bribe.

What holds it: whatever the holder gives, a good harvest left to the people, policing (item 15) that keeps its roads safe, and time, as old takings fade, all raising his standing; and troops in or next to the province, and a governor whose own standing there is high, which keep the moment from ripening. A province that revolts becomes a free power of its own, under its old ruler or the character who led it, with the levies it can raise, and one that revolts with nobody at its head is lawless ("Land without a ruler"); troops of the master in the province fight them as combat says. The owner does not see the number: he learns of unrest as he learns of anything, from his governor (who may misreport it), his spies and travellers, and sees it in the mood of the land ("Who holds what, and the mood of the land" under Interface). First guesses for every weight and the threshold, tuned in build order item 18.

**What is absent on purpose.** No war declarations, no truces, no alliance flags, no opinion meters. A power at peace is simply one nobody is attacking.
